newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-ITALIAN CONTRINI WINS PENULTIMATE STAGE.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-ITALIAN CONTRINI WINS PENULTIMATE STAGE.

text.p: Daniele Contrini of Italy won the sixth stage of the Dunkirk cycle race on Saturday while Belgian world champion Johan Museeuw retained the overall lead with one day to go.
Contrini, who appears to have fully recovered from knee surgery at the end of last season, won the 180.8-km stage from Loon-Plage to the Flandres hills.
The 22-year-old Italian crossed the line ahead of Belgium's Franck Vandenbroucke, who remains second overall, with Ukrainian Andrei Tchmil third.

Museeuw was among a group of six riders who broke away from the peloton in the final sprint, coming in sixth. His lead over Vandenbroucke in the overall standings was cut to 11 seconds and he is 27 ahead of Contrini who moved up to third.

Sunday's flat final 177.4-km stage from Grande-Synthe back to Dunkirk should see Museeuw confirmed as winner for the second time following his victory in 1995, unless his wife gives birth before then and he rushes home early as he announced on Friday.
